newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria outraged by U.S. remarks on Damascus bomb.
newsitem.headline: Syria outraged by U.S. remarks on Damascus bomb.

text.p: Syria on Friday rejected a U.S. warning against blaming Israel for a bomb blast in Damascus that killed nine people and wounded 44 others, saying it was "astonished" by the insensitivity of Washington's remarks.

An official spokesman said a statement by U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns lacked any condemnation of the bombing and did not reflect the fair position required by Washington's role as sponsor of the Middle East peace process.
"Syria was astonished by the statement of the spokesman of the State Department regarding the criminal act which left tens of civilians killed or wounded in Syria," the spokesman said.

"The U.S. spokesman could have disputed the Syrian accusation, but his rush to term it as wild and irresponsible without having evidence for what he is saying is a matter which causes regret and astonishment," he said.

"With his statement, the U.S. spokesman gave the impression his aim was to volunteer to relieve the one who is behind the terrorist action without taking into consideration feelings of the Syrian and Arab people," he said.

Burns said on Thursday the U.S. could not confirm a Syrian report that Israeli agents planted the bus bomb which exploded on Tuesday and warned Damascus against making "wild and irresponsible" statements without evidence.

In response to Syrian complaints Washington on Friday moved to condemn the bus bombing as a terrorist attack and offered condolences to the victims' families. But Burns also repeated criticism of Syria's charge Israel was responsible for the attack.
The Syrian spokesman on Friday renewed the charge that Israel was behind the Damascus bombing. Israel on Friday condemned the bombing and rejected the Syrian accusations first made on Thursday.

"The prime minister (Benjamin Netanyahu) said that the accusations published in Damascus accusing Israel of responsibility for terrorist attacks in Syria are an outright lie. We have no connection to the terrorist attack in Syria and Syria knows it," the Israeli cabinet said in a statement.
But the Syrian spokesman said statements by Israeli officials in recent days included clear threats that Israel would support terrorist actions against Syria and Lebanon.
Last month there were two attacks on Syrian targets in Lebanon. The Lebanese government said Israeli-linked hardline Christians were behind the attacks.
Syria is the main foreign power-broker in Lebanon where it has some 35,000 troops. Israel occupies part of south Lebanon.
Ties between Syria and Israel, who have held sporadic peace talks since 1991, deteriorated severely after Netanyahu took office in June last year.
Syria has said it will not resume the talks, suspended in march by Israel's previous government, until Netanyahu changes his policy of refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace.
